title: A buyer of one shop can post a public 5-star review on a different shop of the same tenant
steps: Place a guest order at mama-ades-kitchen
Vendor completes it
POST /api/v1/public/shops/brixton-village-grill/reviews?email=<buyer email> with {orderId:<Mama Ade's order id>, foodRating:5}
Open /shop/brixton-village-grill
expected: 400: order does not belong to this shop
actual: HTTP 201; Brixton shows '5 (1)' and 'Customer reviews (1)', and its JSON-LD aggregateRating is ratingValue 5, reviewCount 1. ReviewService.createReview checks email, COMPLETED and tenant, but never order.shopId == shop.id
realWorldImpact: A multi-shop owner (or one cheap order) can seed 'verified' ratings on sibling shops. This is a fake-review exposure under DMCC Act 2024 Sch 20 for the platform.

title: The customer's allergen acknowledgement is never sent to or stored by the server
steps: Tick 'I have read the allergen information for this order.' at checkout and place the order
Inspect the POST body
Open the order detail as the vendor
expected: The order record holds acknowledged=true, a timestamp and the allergen set shown
actual: The POST body has no acknowledgement field; no ack field exists in the order DTO or the backend. The gate is client-only, so orders placed through the API or MCP skip it
realWorldImpact: After an allergic reaction the vendor cannot prove the customer was warned, which weakens a due-diligence defence.

title: A vendor cannot say who prepared an order or when; there is no timeline and no export
steps: As admin-user, confirm, start preparation, mark ready and complete an order
Compare the detail before and after
Look for an export or history control in Orders
expected: A timestamped status history with the acting staff user, exportable for a records request
actual: Only status and updatedAt change; createdAt is the only time shown. No actor fields, no export. The Envers audit (revinfo.user_id) is 'kept indefinitely' per /legal/retention, but AuditService is used nowhere
realWorldImpact: A records request from an EHO cannot be answered without a database administrator.

title: No allergen information reaches the customer at or after delivery
steps: Place an order containing allergens
Read all 5 lifecycle emails in Mailhog
View the confirmation and /track
expected: The allergen list goes with the order (email, receipt or label) as distance-selling rules expect
actual: The emails (Received, Confirmed, Being Prepared, Ready, Completed), the confirmation and tracking carry no allergens. The per-product label PDF exists but is not linked to orders
realWorldImpact: The vendor risks an improvement notice; the parent has no written allergen record when the food arrives.

title: An advertised '20% off selected dishes' is never applied
steps: Open /shop/mama-ades-kitchen (banner '20% off selected dishes', chip 'E2E 20% OFF')
Add Jollof Rice and go through to checkout
expected: Discounted dishes are identified and the discount is applied, or the banner is not shown
actual: No dish is marked; Jollof costs £8.99 in the basket, at checkout and in the order record (unitPricePennies 899). Order pricing has no promotion logic
realWorldImpact: A misleading price claim (CPUTR / DMCC Act 2024 Part 4). Customers pay more than advertised.

title: The consumer is never given the seller's legal identity or contact details, or cancellation info; emails present J'Toye as the seller
steps: Read a shop page and checkout
GET /api/v1/public/shops (phone and email are null for all 3 shops)
Read the order emails
expected: Trader identity, geographic address, phone or email, and a no-cancellation statement before purchase and on a durable-medium confirmation (CCR 2013 Sch 2 and reg 16)
actual: Trading name and premises only. No legal entity, company number or VAT-number fields exist. Emails come from noreply@jtoye.uk, are signed '— J'Toye', name no shop and say 'we'll deliver it'. Nothing is said about cancellation
realWorldImpact: After a reaction the consumer can't reach the vendor, and believes J'Toye sold the meal. Advice, then an enforcement order, for both vendor and platform.

title: The privacy notice says the shop is named on the order confirmation; it is not
steps: Read /legal/privacy
Place an order and read the confirmation
actual: The confirmation shows only the order number, payment method and totals
realWorldImpact: The published notice is inaccurate (UK GDPR Art 13 transparency).

title: 'VAT (incl. 20%)' is shown for every vendor, with no VAT-registration status or VAT number captured
steps: Check out at Mama Ade's (onboarding says 'no company number — sole trader')
expected: VAT shown only for VAT-registered vendors, with a VAT number
actual: 'VAT (incl. 20%) £3.83' is shown; no VAT number and no field for one. The legal effect needs legal confirmation
realWorldImpact: An unregistered sole trader appears to charge VAT (HMRC risk).

title: Shop is live although the food-hygiene / FSA registration match failed
steps: As admin-user open /dashboard/onboarding
Compare with the published /shop list
expected: Not published until the check passes, as the page itself states
actual: 'No FSA establishment matched the shop name/address — Manual review', yet the shop is live. No FHRS rating or registration is shown publicly
realWorldImpact: The platform may be listing an unregistered food business. FHRS display is voluntary in England (advice); Wales/NI online display needs legal confirmation.

title: An allergy note asking the shop to confirm goes through to completed with no flag or reply
steps: Order with notes 'My child is allergic to peanuts and sesame - please confirm.'
Vendor confirms and completes it
expected: An allergy note is flagged, needs a vendor response, and the response is recorded
actual: Shown as plain NOTES; nothing records that anyone read it
realWorldImpact: An allergy request can be missed with no trace.

title: A completed cash order stays recorded as 'Payment status NONE / Unpaid'
steps: Complete a cash-on-delivery order
Open its detail

title: Reviews publish the reviewer's full checkout name; no review UI, policy or moderation
steps: View the Brixton review
expected: First name or initial; a published review policy; vendor reporting or moderation
actual: 'Bola Regulator-Test' shown in full; no customer review UI exists and no policy is published
realWorldImpact: Privacy surprise for reviewers; weak DMCC review governance.

title: A cash-only checkout sets Stripe cookies
steps: Check out with cash
Inspect the cookies
expected: No payment-processor cookies when no card payment is possible

title: Record and label detail is weak as evidence: US date format, label use-by taken from the download date, no 'may contain'
steps: Open an order detail
Download a product label
expected: UK date format; use-by from the production date; a cross-contact field
actual: 'Oct 3, 2026, 11:10:25 PM'; 'Use by: 5 Oct 2026' computed when downloaded; no may-contain field
realWorldImpact: Ambiguity in evidence and in labels.

title: Per-line allergen snapshot is recorded at order time and shown to the vendor
steps: Open an order detail as the vendor
expected: The declared allergens as at ordering
actual: Jollof → Celery; Egusi → Crustaceans, Fish; order aggregate shown
realWorldImpact: The vendor can prove what each dish declared on the day.

title: Allergen gate at checkout, plus allergens emphasised per dish and on the PPDS-format label
steps: View dish detail, checkout and the label PDF
actual: Named allergens and a required tick; bold allergens in ingredients; label carries the business name and address
realWorldImpact: Meets the 'before purchase' half of the distance-selling rules.

title: No drip pricing: delivery fee shown on list, menu and basket; total incl. delivery and VAT before ordering
steps: Follow the order journey

title: Reviews are gated to completed orders, a matching email and one per order
steps: Review a pending order; use a wrong email; review the same order twice
actual: 400 'Can only review completed orders'; 400 'You can only review your own orders'; 400 'You have already reviewed this order'
realWorldImpact: A sound base; only the shop check is missing (P2-REG-01).
